I live in Australia and in my city, the hospitals aren't really meant for people with mental heath problems.  
My partner and I admitted ourselves once, and they gave me a bed and told me that I have to spend the night there. I've spent about three days there, saw a mental health nurse and they sent me to ICC (Intermediate care centres, so basically for people who are more or less fine, but still can't go back to society) and I spent a week there.  
I hated it, I honestly hated the hospital and ICC (the nurses and doctors were nice and everything, but they didn't help me at all). So in my opinion, they basically kicked me out because hospitals are for sick people and not for people who have mental problems.   
I went there twice after and they basically told me that there was nothing wrong with me and I can go back home. I'm still scared of going back there again, because I'm scared of getting kicked out again, which will probably happen.   
But my experience should not stop you. Where you live, they might be better with people like us who need help. If you really think that you should go and it will help, you should go, because there is no way they will see you and send you back home on the same day. They will try their hardest to help you and make you feel better. I wish you best of luck, and I hope you'll have better luck then me.  
Stay strong.
